newsitem.title: FINLAND: Question time in Cyberspace for Finnish PM.
newsitem.headline: Question time in Cyberspace for Finnish PM.

text.p: Finnish Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen submitted to over 300 questions from all comers on Tuesday in an Internet session lasting nearly three hours.

"This is fun," wrote Social Democrat Lipponen, whose country has the world's highest number of Internet hosts per head, fielding queries from individuals ranging from international security matters to his sexual orientation.
Government spokesman Mikko Norros said the Prime Minister was not actually typing the answers himself, but dictating them -- sometimes too fast -- to secretaries.
"We aren't censoring anything," he told Reuters by telephone as the session entered its closing minutes with the World Wide Web page (http://www.vn.fi) registering over 120,000 "hits".

People sent their questions -- in Finnish, Swedish and English -- by e-mail on Tuesday afternoon, and the answers were still being fed onto the page at 6.30 p.m. (1630 GMT) as the pace of updates put strain onto the system.

Key issues he addressed included the chance that non-aligned European Union member Finland -- to host a major U.S.-Russian summit on NATO expansion on March 19-20 -- may be preparing to join the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation.
His answer was unoriginal: "Finland is not preparing to join NATO."
Besides complaints about the state of the country and Finland's joblessness, which at around 17 percent is second-highest in the EU, Lipponen took on more private issues.
Recently divorced and publicly dating a younger woman, he was asked when he would marry. The reply: "I haven't decided, nor have I proposed. Should I?"
Asked if he was gay, he said simply "no".
Norros said the object of the exercise, which Lipponen plans to repeat, was partly to highlight the role new technology can play beyond idle social "chat".
"The good thing also is this takes out all the filters -- meaning people like myself or journalists like you," he added.
